claim.excerpt: Analysis of 5,339 cases reported to the National Programme on Substance Abuse Deaths (2000–2019) showed that mean blood cocaine concentrations were approximately 900 ng/mL in cardiac-related deaths, compared with markedly higher levels in acute intoxication (≈19,100 ng/mL) and chronic or binge use (≈6,200 ng/mL).

sources.title: Diagnostic challenges in infant death associated with maternal cocaine abuse during pregnancy and lactation: a forensic case report and review of the literature

why_it_matters: Concentration values are often misread as thresholds; the reviewer must confirm specimen, population, statistic and that the value is reported in context only.
limitations: Approximate means quoted in the introduction of another paper.

concentration_context.population: deaths reported to the National Programme on Substance Abuse Deaths (2000–2019)
concentration_context.case_type: stratified: cardiac-related deaths / acute intoxication / chronic or binge use
limitations: Approximate means quoted in the introduction of another paper.

reviewer_checklist: Excerpt matches the source at the stated location.
Proposed value says no more than the excerpt.
Source is current (not retracted/superseded) and the licence allows this use.
Context and limitations are complete; nothing is presented as a threshold.
